questions: Did progress hold at or above 0.1604 on the s-bend and 0.110 on the slalom, matching iteration 9?
Did max_error stay at or below 0.069 on every track, particularly the slalom (0.0676 last race)? If not, at what progress does the robot leave the track?
Did noise_robustness change from the disturbance and sensor noise, and is it low enough to suggest the final unseen track could push the robot off the line?
Did any run finish, and if so, what is the completion_time?

intent: Hold the iteration 9 best geometry (wheel_radius 0.044 m, all else unchanged) and confirm that its result is repeatable with the Integrator's controller. I expect s-bend progress at or above 0.158, slalom at or above 0.110, and max_error at or below 0.069 on every track. No further geometry step is planned unless this holds, in which case the remaining gains belong to the controller.
learning: Wheel radius 0.03 to 0.044 m has raised progress in small steps with max_error held or only slightly raised (s-bend 0.149 to 0.155 to 0.158 to 0.1604). The gain per step is shrinking, and the slalom max_error is near the band. Further geometry gains are unlikely to be worth the risk, so the final geometry should be wheel_radius 0.044 m unless this confirmation race shows max_error above 0.069, in which case 0.04 m is the fallback.
rationale: Iteration 9 (wheel_radius 0.044 m, all else as iteration 8) is the best result so far at 52.14. Progress rose on the s-bend (0.158 to 0.1604) and the slalom (0.1075 to 0.110), and max_error fell on the s-bend (0.0684 to 0.0617). The slalom max_error rose slightly (0.0634 to 0.0676) but stayed under the 0.069 band, and the oval was unchanged at progress 0.11 and max_error 0.062. This meets the stated keep-speed condition: progress above 0.158 on the s-bend and 0.1075 on the slalom, with max_error at or below 0.069 on every track. Speed is still helping, but returns are shrinking. The 0.04 to 0.044 m step gave about +0.0024 progress on the s-bend and +0.0025 on the slalom. The slalom max_error is now 0.0676, close to the 0.069 band. A further step to 0.048 m would probably push the slalom past that band for a small gain, and an unseen final track may have tighter bends. I therefore hold wheel_radius at 0.044 m and keep mass 0.6 kg, wheel_track 0.12 m and the 12 mm sensor layout at x = -0.03 to 0.03 m, y = 0.04 m. Iterations 0 to 8 showed that sensor, body, track and mass changes do not help, so this iteration confirms the best geometry and leaves the remaining gains to the controller. I added noise_robustness to the measurements because the final track is unseen and robustness to the fixed motor mismatch and sensor noise now matters more than small progress gains.
